rawFindings.title: --save-exact drops non-registry source from saved dependency
rawFindings.explanation: When installing a package from a path or URL with both --save and --save-exact, this line overwrites the dependency entry with only the resolved version. For non-registry endpoints that loses the original source, so the saved bower.json no longer describes the package that was installed.
rawFindings.suggestion: Preserve the source for non-registry endpoints, e.g. write `decEndpoint.source + '#' + decEndpoint.pkgMeta.version` when `decEndpoint.name !== decEndpoint.source`, and only write the bare version for registry packages.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Run `bower install /tmp/private-pkg --save --save-exact` where `/tmp/private-pkg/bower.json` has `{ "name": "private-pkg", "version": "1.2.3" }` and the package is not in the registry. The new bower.json saves `"private-pkg": "1.2.3"`; a later `bower install` tries to resolve `private-pkg#1.2.3` from the registry instead of `/tmp/private-pkg#1.2.3`, failing or installing the wrong package.
